notes: Shot 17 peacock barbules: the effective-medium multilayer of Freyer & Stavenga 2020 (Faraday Discuss. 223:49-62, doi 10.1039/D0FD00033G; ref/peacock/papers/optics_Freyer_Stavenga_2020_tail.pdf), which they fitted to measured MSP spectra of the six eye regions (their Fig. 6).

Model (their Materials and methods, p. 51-52): keratin cortex c on top, then Nm layers of melanosomes (rods, diameter Dm, depth period a, lateral period b) with air channels (diameter Da) between them; sliced into thin layers, each with volume fractions fk, fm, fa and n_eff = (fk nk^w + fm nm^w + fa na^w)^(1/w), w_TE 2.5, w_TM -1.5 (their FDTD-adjusted values, p. 52; the minus is lost in the PDF text, read from the research report and two-phase EMT w_TM = -2); unpolarised = mean of TE and TM.
keratin nk = 1.532 + 5890/lam^2 (Leertouwer 2011, via Freyer p. 51); melanin nm = 1.648 + 23700/lam^2, km = 0.56 exp(-lam/270) (Stavenga 2015, via Freyer p. 51-52).

[A] ours: air channels centred midway between rod layers (Nm-1 of them; Zi 2003's air holes sit in the centre of the rod lattice's cells); the substrate under the stack is keratin and what enters it is lost (Freyer p. 55: the lower stack and the interior's random melanosomes add 'at most a very small fraction'); slices 2 nm.

Per-barbule spread (the table's s axis) is the lattice period a, over the anatomical ranges Freyer's Table 1 lists (R2: Durrer 157-175, Jiang 153-178, Yoshioka 150, Zi 150; R3: Durrer 198-223, Zi/Li 185, Medina 198); the other parameters stay at Freyer's model values. How a is distributed over the barbules is [A].

amplitude_scale [F]: the tables of R3 are scaled by 0.44 relative to R2 so their peak ratio is Freyer Fig. 5's probe ratio (R3 0.06 / R2 0.24 measured, vs 0.20 / 0.35 from this model at the model a): the model alone makes the brown ring ~2.3x too bright against the blue-green zone. Why the model over-predicts R3 is not resolved (tilted / disordered cells, Freyer p. 58). r1 then lowered it to 0.33 [F]: with 0.44 the ring came out +10 codes and the zone -7 against the original, and the shared lights cannot move one without the other; 0.33 is a fit to the original, 0.44 the measured ratio.

R2_blue_green.source: Freyer 2020 Table 1 R2 'Model'; measured peak 500 nm (p. 56, Fig. 5b)

R3_brown.source: Freyer 2020 Table 1 R3 'Model'; measured peaks 530 and 660 nm (p. 56, Fig. 5c)

R4_green_yellow.source: Freyer 2020 Table 1 R4 'Model'; measured peak 600 nm (p. 56, Fig. 5d); used only as a check

tilt.source: Yoshioka & Kinoshita 2002 (Forma 17:169-181) Fig. 7: the tilt of the barbules' multilayer, Gaussian exp(-t^2/theta0^2), theta0 15 deg, reproduces their angle-resolved spectra
